---
title: "multised (merged)"
subtitle: "The single merged marine-sediment database"
---

**multised** assembles a database of marine-sediment trace-element measurements from
five external sources, harmonises them into a common schema, and progressively
quality-controls the result. This site presents the **final product**: a single
**merged** database that combines all five sources into one, together with the
Norwegian **aquaculture** reference database paired with it.

The earlier stages are documented on their own sites:

- how each source is reshaped and quality-flagged (the **slim** stage) is on the
  [slim site](https://seafood-hazards.github.io/multised-slim/);
- how the flags are applied to build the **clean** databases, and the analyses
  performed on them (grain size, Fe/Al normalisation, organic carbon, and the
  cross-source merge itself) are on the
  [clean-analyses site](https://seafood-hazards.github.io/multised-clean/).

## The two databases

```{r}
library(tibble)
library(knitr)

tribble(
  ~Database,                  ~Contents,
  "multised_merged.sqlite",   "All five sources combined into one, with cross-source duplicates removed (one row per reading). Bulk and sieved kept as separate tracks.",
  "aquaculture_no.sqlite",    "Norwegian marine aquaculture sites (active and closed), used to tag each Norwegian sediment site with its distance to the nearest farm."
) |> kable()
```

## Pipeline generations

The data moves through five generations, one SQLite database **per source** until the
merge, then a single database from there:

1. **pilot**: each source's raw files parsed into a per-source database. Documented on
   the individual pilot sites:
   [Mareano](https://seafood-hazards.github.io/mareano-pilot/),
   [Vannmiljø](https://seafood-hazards.github.io/vannmiljo-pilot/),
   [ICES-DOME](https://seafood-hazards.github.io/ices-dome-pilot/),
   [MUDAB](https://seafood-hazards.github.io/mudab-pilot/), and
   [4Demon](https://seafood-hazards.github.io/4demon-pilot/).
2. **slim**: every source reshaped into the same seven-table schema, then annotated
   with quality-control flags. Documented on the
   [slim site](https://seafood-hazards.github.io/multised-slim/).
3. **clean**: the flags are applied (uncertain rows removed), units harmonised, and
   grain-size split into its own table. Five per-source databases. Documented on the
   [clean-analyses site](https://seafood-hazards.github.io/multised-clean/).
4. **merged** *(this site)*: the five clean databases are combined into a single
   `multised_merged.sqlite`, with cross-source duplicates removed.
5. **refined** *(creation documented on this site)*: a restructured, slimmed copy of
   the merged database with the reusable analysis results baked in, an analysis-ready
   base for the pristine / background-sediment work. Its build is documented here (the
   [Refined DB](./refined-schema.qmd) pages) and the analyses on the
   [refined site](https://seafood-hazards.github.io/multised-refined/).

## What this site covers

**DB Design**: the table layouts, with entity-relationship diagrams.

- [DB Schema (Merged)](./db-schema-merged.qmd): the merged database.
- [DB Schema (Aquaculture)](./db-schema-aquaculture.qmd): the aquaculture reference.

**Analyses** on the merged database (bulk samples, outliers dropped):

- [Data Categories](./data-categories.qmd): measurement counts per element, by
  fraction, covariate availability and layering, with the analyses each subset supports.
- [Outlier Flagging](./outlier-flagging.qmd): the soft `outlier_flag` marking values
  implausibly far from their element's distribution (mostly registration errors).
- [Grain Size](./grain-size.qmd): how bulk concentrations track the mud (fines) content.
- [Fe/Al Normalisation](./normalisation.qmd): metals against their lithogenic carriers,
  iron and aluminium.
- [Organic Carbon](./organic-carbon.qmd): metals against organic carbon.
- [Depth Profiles](./depth-profile.qmd): how concentrations change down a core.
- [Bulk vs Sieved](./enrichment.qmd): how much the sieved fraction concentrates metals
  over bulk.
- [Depth and Coast](./spatial.qmd): enrichment and covariates against water depth and
  distance to coast.
- [Sampling Year](./temporal.qmd): whether a trend over sampling year survives
  normalisation.
- [Repeat-Sampled Sites](./site-years.qmd): temporal trends within locations sampled in
  several years, with location held roughly fixed.

**Clustering** looks for unsupervised structure across the merged chemistry:

- [Geochemical Facies](./geochemical-facies.qmd): multi-element signatures in chemistry
  space (K-means).
- [Spatial Hotspots](./spatial-hotspots.qmd): where elevated readings cluster
  geographically (DBSCAN).
- [Geochemical Regions](./geochemical-regions.qmd): clustering on location and
  composition together.

**Explore** browses the databases in the page, with no server (the SQLite files run
in the browser via WebAssembly):

- [Merged Tables](./merged-tables.qmd) and
  [Aquaculture Tables](./aquaculture-tables.qmd): paginated table browsers.
- [Element Map](./element-map.qmd): trace elements, normalisers and organic carbon
  per site (bulk or sieved).
- [Location Map](./location-map.qmd): site depth, distance to coast, and distance to
  aquaculture.
- [Grain Size Map](./grain-size-map.qmd): bulk and sieved (<63 µm, <20 µm) sample
  locations.
- [Aquaculture Map](./aquaculture-map.qmd): the Norwegian aquaculture sites, active
  and closed.

**Refined DB**: how a fifth, refined generation is built from the merged database, an
analysis-ready database for the later pristine / background-sediment work.

- [DB Schema (Refined)](./refined-schema.qmd): the refined table layout and what changed.
- [Building the Refined DB](./refined-build.qmd): the step-by-step transformation and
  what is kept.

::: {.callout-note}
How the merged database is built, step by step (union, deduplication, finalise) and
how the aquaculture table is created are documented on the
[clean-analyses site](https://seafood-hazards.github.io/multised-clean/).
:::
